Hi Ana / AWS team —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. OrbitHealth is looking to move forward with a Private Offer that spans US commercial and an EU node (three-year commit). Two operational asks came up that we need to lock down before pricing:

1) Regionally weighted discount: Orbit wants a blended discount that reflects higher list prices in the EU region (not a flat % across all SKUs). Do we have an accepted way to show a per-region multiplier in the Private Offer so the customer sees a single effective discount but we preserve per-region listprice linkage on the backend?

2) Partner margin routing: Orbit will purchase through ResellCo (EU distributor). They want the partner rebate/commission to be passed to ResellCo directly at invoice time rather than via a separate rebate. Can the private-offer billing path be configured so AWS invoices to Orbit but the reseller margin is passed through to ResellCo (invoice or settlement note)? Any constraints on how that shows up in the Marketplace invoice (line items vs separate credit)?

Attached: a draft MA proposal and a small CSV mapping proposed regional multipliers per SKU. Can you confirm operational constraints and any AWS Marketplace fields we need to include in the offer feed?

If helpful, I can loop in Laura (rev ops) and Jordan (partner ops) — I’ve CC'd Irene who is our lead on channel flows.

Next step: would appreciate a short note from AWS by EOD with the supported patterns and any evidence/links we should include in Orbit’s procurement packet.

Thanks,

Hi Ben / Ana —

Thanks for the clear note. Short answers up front:

- Per-region multipliers: AWS Private Offers support custom pricing per AWS region via the Offer API. You can present an effective blended discount to the buyer, but the backend will record region-specific list price / discounted price pairs. The way we recommend is to include a region_price_override table in the private-offer payload; that maintains traceability for auditing.

- Partner margin routing: Marketplace doesn't currently support a single invoice that splits payment automatically to a third-party reseller at invoice time. Typical patterns are:
  1) AWS invoices the buyer and issues a separate settlement to the reseller (our settlement pipeline can be configured to route reseller payouts to a marketplace partner account), or
  2) The reseller invoices the buyer separately and Redwood provides a rebate line item on your side to reconcile.

Option 1 is usually cleaner for the partner; it requires the reseller to be onboarded as a Marketplace seller/distributor (Marta copied here). Option 2 is sometimes used where regulatory/tax rules prevent direct settlement.

I've attached the guide to the offer feed fields and the seller onboarding checklist. If ResellCo is willing to be configured as a distributor in the EU node, we can loop Legal/Finance to define settlement timing.

Best,
AWS Marketplace Sales
attachments: aws_private_offer_fields.pdf (pdf), seller_onboarding_checklist.pdf (pdf)

Ben — quick internal read and recommended path. Keeping it tight so we can reply to Orbit with an actionable proposal.

Summary of constraints from AWS:
- We can present a blended discount at the offer level, but AWS will still require per-region price entries for audit.
- Direct split-at-invoice requires reseller onboarded as Marketplace seller/distributor. Otherwise settlements are post-invoice.

Suggested approach (one-pager we can send to Orbit):
1) Pricing: accept AWS region_price_override pattern. We create a single "Effective Discount" % in the MA for customer-facing documentation and include the region_discount_matrix.csv as the appendix so procurement can reconcile list prices. That satisfies audit and keeps the procurement packet simple.

2) Partner margin routing: recommend Option 1 (reseller onboarding) as the primary path. Operational steps:
   - Ask ResellCo to start Marketplace distributor onboarding (Marta).
   - If onboarding takes longer than 2-3 weeks, use fallback: Redwood issues a partner rebate (quarterly credit) that appears as a separate credit memo to Orbit and a contractual side letter guaranteeing pass-through to ResellCo.

3) Accounting/tax: require revenue ops (Laura) to confirm tax treatment on EU settlements; we may need to adjust gross-to-net mapping for EMEA.

4) Next steps and asks for Ben to include in reply to Orbit: commitment floors by region (node hours / $/year), any legal constraints on reseller invoicing, and confirmation of desired visible discount vs backend mapping.

If everyone agrees, I’ll draft the short customer-facing note and a fallback template for the credit memo.

Irene Choi
Head of Marketplace Partnerships — Redwood Inference
